item.text:
This turn closed the last feasible executed-coverage gap.

**Transport layer now actually executed (no sockets needed)**
The deadlock was my harness not draining the pipeline's unbuffered `doneCh` — that's the documented back-pressure, not an implementation bug. After fixing that, [zz_audit_transport_test.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_19-48-15-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/zz_audit_transport_test.go) drives `net_transport.go` through a `net.Pipe`-backed fake `StreamLayer`:

- generic request/response path: `AppendEntries`, `RequestVote`, `RequestPreVote`, `TimeoutNow`
- the heartbeat fast-path handler (heartbeat-shaped `AppendEntries` bypasses the consumer channel)
- `InstallSnapshot` request + streamed payload
- the pipelined `AppendEntries` path

Result: **PASS**, stable over `-count=20`, and **PASS under `-race`** with no data race. Combined with all three audit tests: `go test -race -run 'TestAudit_'` → ok (24s), log `logs/audit_transport.log`.

**Status of findings:** still no concrete correctness defect. Provenance (byte-identical to official `hashicorp/raft@v1.7.3`), the in-repo suite, static checks, the repeated `-race` sweep, the in-memory crash/restart test, the randomized acknowledged-entries safety check, and now executed transport coverage all support that. `net_transport.go`/`tcp_transport.go` were also reviewed line-by-line.

**Remaining unexecuted coverage:** only the literal TCP tests (`TestNetworkTransport_*`, `TestTCPTransport_*`) and the `fuzzy` linearizability suite — both require AF_INET, which this shell forbids, and the `isolated_exec` tool still won't dispatch from my side. Everything is recorded in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_19-48-15-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).
